summary_paragraph: A 68-year-old woman with a history of Crohn’s disease, alcoholic cirrhosis, peptic ulcer disease, coronary artery disease, and heart failure was admitted for bright red blood per rectum. She presented after experiencing multiple large-volume bloody bowel movements over two days, with a drop in hemoglobin from 34.8 to 27.0. She received two units of packed red blood cells with incomplete response and was transferred to the ICU for central venous access due to limited peripheral IV access. A colonoscopy revealed internal hemorrhoids and diverticulosis but no active colonic bleeding. After restarting aspirin, she had one additional episode of bleeding, prompting a capsule endoscopy, which showed no source in the small intestine. Her hemoglobin stabilized, and she was discharged home in stable condition. Medications were adjusted, including holding aspirin and Plavix, reducing Toprol to 25 mg daily, and continuing home therapies for Crohn’s and diabetes with instructions to taper insulin back to baseline.
problems: Internal hemorrhoids without mention of complication
Diverticulosis of colon (without mention of hemorrhage)
Diabetes mellitus without mention of complication, type II or unspecified type, not stated as uncontrolled
Hypertensive chronic kidney disease, unspecified, with chronic kidney disease stage I through stage IV, or unspecified
Coronary atherosclerosis of native coronary artery
Personal history of venous thrombosis and embolism
